query: The Co-free FeNiCrMn system was selected to reduce cost while retaining the mechanical performance of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi; prior work reported comparable or better mechanical properties after excluding Co. Research on FeNiCrMn has mainly addressed corrosion, while studies of related high- and medium-entropy alloys examined dynamic responses under tension or compression, different temperatures and strain rates, compositional changes, and the presence of cracks or voids. Those studies established that dynamic properties are sensitive to loading regime and material condition, but their different chemistries and defect states do not identify what governs FeNiCrMn. Under the constraints of retaining the Co-free composition and its strength–ductility balance, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis explains the dynamic behavior of solidified FeNiCrMn across temperature and strain-rate regimes? Define a controlled study capable of testing the hypothesis, its applicable boundaries, the prior findings that support it, and a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The dynamic behavior of solidified FeNiCrMn across temperature and strain-rate regimes is governed by the formation of adiabatic shear bands (ASBs) and the resulting grain refinement and increase in dislocation density.
generation.intervention: Variation of temperature and strain rate
generation.mechanism: Grain refinement and increase in dislocation density due to ASB formation
generation.predicted_outcome: Enhanced mechanical properties, including strength and ductility, at high strain rates and temperatures
generation.boundary: Temperature range: -200°C to 500°C, strain rate range: 10^-3 s^-1 to 10^3 s^-1
generation.uncertainty: The exact relationship between ASB formation and mechanical properties is still unclear and requires further investigation

falsification_experiment.design: Compression tests using split-Hopkinson pressure bar (SHPB) at various strain rates and temperatures
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If no ASBs are observed in the microstructure and the mechanical properties do not exhibit significant enhancement at high strain rates and temperatures, the hypothesis is falsified

There has been an increase in experimental and computational studies on the dynamic response of HEAs in recent years. Dynamic experiments [,,,,,] were performed using different methods, including split-Hopkinson bars, light-gas guns, and laser shock facilities, to achieve strain rates ranging from 103 to 107/s. For example, in the study conducted by Zhao et al. [], quasi-static compression and dynamic shearing were applied to the equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA. They observed a dense structure, which consisted of stacking faults, deformation twins, and phase transformations from face-centered cubic (FCC) to HCP, as well as amorphous structures. Yang et al. [] investigated the shock loading of the Cr10Mn10Fe60Co10Ni10 HEA, and they observed two phase transformations: from FCC to hexagonal close-packed (HCP) and from FCC to body-centered cubic (BCC) structures. Thürmer et al. [] studied the shock-induced spallation of the CrMnFeCoNi HEA using a high-power laser. Their results indicated that the deformation mechanism of the material was primarily dominated by nanoscale mechanical twinning at elevated strain rates. Currently, several EHEA systems have been developed, including AlCoCrFeNi2.1 [], Al17Ni34Ti17V32 [], AlCr1.3TiNi2 [], and AlCrCuFeNi2 []. Owing to better practicality and low cost, the AlCrFe2Ni2 alloy, with similar microstructure and properties to the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy, was investigated. It is indicated that the AlCrFe2Ni2 alloy consists of the FCC and A2/B2 spinodal decomposition phase and presents better fracture strength and ductility []. In addition, the dynamic mechanical response of HEAs has also received a lot of attention. To use HEAs in extreme industrial environments, there is an urgent need for a comprehensive understanding of their performance and mechanisms during high-speed compression [,,,,]. According to the available literature, in addition to the dislocation-related mechanism, twinning mechanism, grain boundary-related mechanism, diffusion creep mechanism, and dynamic recrystallization mechanism, the shear bands are formed in HEAs at high strain rates or under large deformation conditions [,,,,].
